chunks: And what is in it from Malik Al-Juhani, I have narrated it from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far Al-Kumandani, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Muhammad Malik ibn A'yan Al-Juhani
He was an Arab from Kufa, and he is not from the family of Sansan.

key_terms.آلُ سَنْسَنَ: The family of Sansan, a distinct lineage used for disambiguation
key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to the author, Ibn Babawayh)
key_terms.الْكُمَنْدَانِيُّ: Al-Kumandani, a nisba indicating origin or lineage of Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far
key_terms.عَرَبِيٌّ كُوفِيٌّ: Arab from Kufa, describing the narrator's ethnicity and residence
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُوسَى: Ali ibn Musa (Imam al-Rida), a key link in the chain

ai.seo_question: Who is Malik Al-Juhani and how is he distinguished from other narrators with the same name?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous biographical scrutiny (ilm al-rijal) characteristic of Shia hadith scholarship, specifically addressing the common issue of name duplication (tashabuh) among narrators. By distinguishing this Malik ibn Ayn al-Juhani as an Arab from Kufa and not from the family of Sansan, Shaykh al-Saduq ensures the authenticity of the chain leading back to Imam Ali al-Rida, thereby preserving the integrity of the transmitted knowledge.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Everything in this book that is narrated from Malik Al-Juhani has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah (swt) be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Musa ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Ja'far Al-Kamandani, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam, from Abu Muhammad Malik ibn A'yan Al-Juhani.
He was an Arab from Kufa and not from the family of Sansan.
